description: The Supreme Court of India is the apex judicial authority of the country. It serves as the final interpreter and guardian of the Indian Constitution, and acts as the guarantor of the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.

sections.title: Establishment and Historical Background
sections.description: Key facts regarding the inception and historical evolution of the Supreme Court in India.

historical_events.significance: Led to the establishment of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Calcutta in 1774, which consisted of one Chief Justice and three other judges.
Provided for the establishment of the 'Federal Court of India' in 1937, which possessed original and appellate jurisdiction.
The Supreme Court of independent India was inaugurated, replacing both the Federal Court of India and the British Privy Council.

important_facts.fact: The first Chief Justice of independent India was H. J. Kania.
As per the 2026 Ordinance, the maximum sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court was increased to 38 judges (1 Chief Justice + 37 other judges).

sections.title: Important Constitutional Provisions
sections.description: Articles 124 to 147 in Part V (Chapter 4) of the Indian Constitution deal with the organization, independence, jurisdiction, powers, and procedures of the Supreme Court.

polity_articles.provision: Establishment and Constitution of Supreme Court
polity_articles.details: Details the appointment, qualifications, and removal (impeachment) process of the judges.
The judgments of the Supreme Court are kept as records for evidentiary value, and it has the power to punish for its contempt.
Handles disputes directly between the Centre and States or among States. This concept is inspired by the US Constitution.
Grants the Supreme Court the power to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it.
Authorizes the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance.

sections.title: Appointment and Functioning of Judges
sections.description: The procedures for the appointment of judges, their qualifications, and provisions for special appointments.

key_concepts.explanation: A system for the appointment and transfer of judges that evolved through the 'Three Judges Cases'. It comprises the Chief Justice of India and a forum of the 4 senior-most judges of the Supreme Court.
Under Article 126, the President can appoint a judge of the Supreme Court as an Acting Chief Justice when the office of CJI is vacant or the CJI is absent.

Under Article 127, if there is a lack of quorum to hold or continue a session, the CJI can appoint a High Court judge as an ad-hoc judge of the Supreme Court for a temporary period, with prior consent from the President.

important_facts.fact: The Constitution has not prescribed a minimum age for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court, but they hold office until they attain the age of 65 years.
A judge can be removed from office by the President only after a motion of impeachment is passed by both Houses of Parliament with a special majority, based on 'proved misbehaviour' or 'incapacity'.

sections.title: Powers and Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
sections.description: The extensive judicial powers granted to the Supreme Court to dispense justice and protect constitutional rights.

key_concepts.explanation: Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue 5 types of writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto) for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
It is the highest court of appeal in the country, hearing appeals against judgments of High Courts in constitutional, civil, and criminal matters (Articles 132, 133, 134).
The power of the Supreme Court to examine the constitutionality of legislative enactments and executive orders. If found violative of the Constitution, they can be declared 'null and void'.

polity_articles.details: The Supreme Court is authorized to grant in its discretion special leave to appeal from any judgment in any matter passed by any court or tribunal in the territory of India.
Allows the Supreme Court to pass any decree or make any order necessary for doing 'complete justice' in any cause or matter pending before it.

sections.title: Important Judicial Doctrines and Facts
sections.description: Landmark judgments, significant doctrines established by the Court, and other crucial exam-oriented facts.

key_associations.extra_info: The Supreme Court ruled that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, but it cannot destroy its 'basic structure'. This case was decided by the largest ever 13-Judge Bench.

key_associations.item: P. N. Bhagwati & V. R. Krishna Iyer
key_associations.extra_info: They introduced PIL in India during the 1980s, which relaxed the traditional rule of 'Locus Standi' to allow public-spirited individuals to approach the courts on behalf of the disadvantaged.

important_facts.fact: Justice Fathima Beevi was the first female judge of the Supreme Court, appointed in 1989.

A bench consisting of at least 5 judges is constituted to hear cases involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution; this is known as a 'Constitution Bench' (Article 145(3)).
Justice Surya Kant took oath as the 53rd Chief Justice of India in November 2025.
